title: slice-gating-and-communal-ops-contract-sketch-wip
content:
Context:

This is a working sketch for a communal ops contract that sits between Product, SRE, and Solutions/SE teams for gating slices during staggered rollouts and A/B experiments. The goal is to codify minimal human checkpoints, automated signal thresholds, and clearly owned reversion/mitigation actions so cross-functional teams can move faster with bounded risk.

Why this is different from other rollout notes:
- Focus is on the "contract" (who signs what) rather than detailed traffic partition heuristics.
- Emphasizes lightweight human checkpoints and explicit ticket/comms artifacts that get created automatically when gates trip.
- Provides templates for on-call/responder behavior and escalation cadence.

High level principles (working):
1) Minimal human gates: prefer automated pass/fail where possible; human inspection only when signal ambiguity > 20%.
2) Ownership clarity: every stage has a primary owner (Product PM), secondary owner (SRE or Solutions depending on impact), and an escalation lead (Eng manager).
3) Immutable experiment artifact: every slice activation produces a single, immutable run artifact (config + hash + timestamp) stored in rollout-configs repo.
4) Fast reversion: plan for an automatic rollback if critical SLOs breach for more than N minutes (default N=3).
5) Observability baked in: synthetic probes, sample traces, and token-level cost deltas shipped as part of activation.

Roles and responsibilities (proposed):
- Product PM (primary): defines slice, hypotheses, guardrails, acceptance metrics, stakeholder comms.
- SRE (secondary): defines runbook, ensures monitoring/alerting hooks, confirms safety of rollout infra.
- Solutions / Sales Eng (secondary for enterprise canaries): provides customer-facing risk assessments and optional gating for high-visibility customers.
- Oncall Eng (escalation): triages alerts and drives mitigations or hotfixes.
- Steward (rotation, often product ops): runs the checklist, marks gates as manually inspected if required, files the incident/ticket when a gate trips.

Gates and signal taxonomy (practical):
- Critical gates (automatic rollback if triggered): error rate (5xx or model runtime error), token latency tail (p95 > baseline * 2.0), cost-per-token spike (> 3x expected), privacy/security alerts.
- High-priority gates (require human ack and 15 min assessment window): user-facing quality regressions (measured by evaluation harness on seeded prompts), significant drift in embed distances for top queries, increased hallucination rate on monitoring prompts.
- Informational signals (dashboard-only): small latency variance, throughput variance within expected range, token-mix shifts.

Default thresholds (example baseline aware):
- p95 latency > 2x historical baseline for 3 continuous 1-minute windows -> CRITICAL
- 5xx rate > 0.5% and absolute increase > 0.2% vs baseline -> CRITICAL
- Eval harness failure rate increase > 4 percentage points vs pre-release -> HIGH

Activation flow (fast path):
1) PM uploads rollout artifact to rollout-configs and triggers a canary activation via Console. Artifact includes: model_version, config_hash, cohort_selector, traffic_percent, start_time, roll_forward_policy.
2) Console provisions canary slice and wires monitoring dashboards + synthetic probe job.
3) System automatically routes initial traffic slab (default 0.5%) and starts automated checks for first 10 minutes.
4) If no Crit gates fire, automated schedule advances to pre-agreed slab (e.g., 5%) with another hold period (30m).
5) At each hold, Steward receives a summary email + Slack ephemeral post with 10-signal summary and an action button: PROCEED / PAUSE & INVESTIGATE / ROLL BACK.

Human-checkpoint flow (when invoked):
- Steward inspects the artifact and the dashboard. If ambiguous signals, Steward sets a 30-minute manual hold and notifies stakeholders using the template below.
- If confirmed issue: steward triggers ROLLBACK (Console API) and opens JIRA with template.

Automated actions and ticketing (contract):
- On Crit gate trip -> Console auto-initiates rollback and creates JIRA ticket: prefix ROLLBACK-<artifact_hash>. Slack alert posted to #rollouts with incident snippet.
- On High-priority gate trip -> Console auto-creates JIRA: INVEST-<artifact_hash>, notifies Steward and SRE oncall; rollback is not automatic but recommended.
- For informational signals -> annotated in rollout artifact; no tickets created.

Communication templates (copy/paste):
- Slack initial: "[Rollout] activation started: artifact %s, cohort %s, slab %s%%. Steward: %s. Dash: %s. Expected hold time: %s. PM: %s"
- Slack gate trip: "[ROLLBACK TRIGGERED] artifact %s triggered %s at %s. Action: rollback executed. Jira: %s. Pager: %s. Primary contacts: %s"
- JIRA summary template (ROLLBACK-<hash>): Title: "Rollback: artifact <hash> — automatic rollback triggered"; Description: short artifact details, triggered metric/time windows, first 5 sample traces, follow-ups required.

Example rollout artifact (plain text snippet stored with run):
{"model_version":"open-7b-v2", "artifact_hash":"a1f3b7", "cohort_selector":"country in (US,CA) AND user_activity > 10", "traffic_percent":"0.5 -> 5 -> 25 -> 100", "synthetic_probes":"seeded-llm-smoke-v2", "monitoring_dash":"/dash/rollouts/a1f3b7"}

Note: the snippet above is for human readability. The actual artifact is JSON persisted in the rollout-configs repo and immutable after activation.

Observability checklist (must be present before activation):
- Synthetic probes (smoke + quality) running at 1m cadence against seeded prompt set (10 prompts).
- End-to-end latency p50/p95/p99 visualization for the last 2 hours baseline + real-time pull.
- Error logs tagged to artifact hash; ability to fetch 50 sample traces within 2 min.
- Token cost delta per request computed and emitted as metric.
- Eval harness (offline) run with a sample of production-like prompts and stored results compared to baseline.

Escalation playbook (short):
1) Crit gate auto-rollback -> Steward files JIRA and posts to #rollouts; SRE paged and triage within 15m.
2) If rollback fails or infra degradation concurrent -> SRE oncall declares incident, escalate to oncall manager and Backend Eng.
3) Product PM drafts customer comms if customer-facing cohort included; Solutions Eng coordinates customer outreach.

Metrics to include in the snapshot (minimum):
- Traffic volume (requests/min) for slice
- p50/p95/p99 latency
- 5xx and model-runtime error rate
- Synthetic probe score (pass/fail and percent correct)
- Embedding distance drift for top-100 queries
- Token cost per request and per-token delta vs baseline

Open questions / discussion items (please add):
- Should we make rollback threshold time window configurable per experiment? (tradeoff: flexibility vs cognitive overhead)
- Where is the single source of truth for baseline? (dash vs offline metrics store)
- Do we allow targeted customer-level pauses (e.g., pause only for customers A,B) or only cohort-level?

Next steps (owner assigned):
- Rina: sketch Console UI for Steward inline action buttons (PROCEED/PAUSE/ROLLBACK) — due 2024-12-08.
- Diego: add immutable artifact write to rollout-configs repo with schema + hash — due 2024-12-01.
- Owen: prototype auto-ticketing flow and Slack formatting — due 2024-12-05.
- Leah (owner): gather feedback from SRE and Solutions and reconvene — check-in 2024-12-06.

Notes to self / quick heuristics (choppy):
- default tiny slab 0.5% is helpful for networked features where errors cascade
- synthetic probes should be owned by product but executed by SRE infra job
- always include sample traces in the ticket, otherwise triage stalls

References and links:
- See rollout-configs repo PR for immutable artifact format: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-configs/pull/219
- Related canary safety checklists live in Console playbooks (confluence id CONFLUENCE-1234)
